prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1125; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a collision at an intersection. Insured vehicle was turning left when it was struck by a vehicle traveling straight through. Insured reports minimal damage to the driver side and no airbag deployment. Police report requested. Liability appears to lean toward the other driver, pending statements.

Entry 2: Claimant's attorney's office sent a letter of representation today. All further contact regarding the claimant to be routed through counsel. Claimant has reported neck and back strain and has begun treatment with a chiropractor. Medical records and billing requested through counsel. Reserve set for bodily injury pending review of records.

Entry 3: Spoke with insured to confirm the sequence of events. Insured states the light had changed to green for the oncoming traffic and they had entered the intersection to turn left on a yellow arrow. Insured acknowledges they did not see the other vehicle until impact. Dashcam footage not available. Recorded statement scheduled.

Entry 4: Received copy of the police report. Responding officer cited the other driver for failure to yield on a red signal, though the citation is pending. Witness statement from a nearby pedestrian is included and supports the insured's account of the signal phase. Liability assessment updated to favor insured at a high percentage, subject to confirmation of the signal timing from the city.

Entry 5: Counsel for claimant responded to the liability position and disputes that the claimant was at fault. Counsel requested the full claim file and a copy of the insured's policy declarations. Advised that the file will be released only as permitted under the policy and applicable law. Supervisor notified of the attorney involvement and the bodily injury component. Next step is to review treatment records once received and evaluate the injury claim.
